Content: So AI is mainly software than can understand more human search terms, and sometimes more complex agorithms to provide context based options. I think bolting the term onto literally everything these days is misleading. Does the software 'learn' from prior interactions to both improve its own functionality as well as the way it understands human inputs? If not, then it's not AI - it's just software enhancement. I guess if everyone else is throwing the term around, and the term has some grey areas around definition then you may as well call your new search function AI or you'll get potentially left behind. Clever change to detect a postcode and auto look up house-owner details is not AI, it's just a lookup function but what do you lose by calling it that, when everyone has lost their mind and will punish you if you called it what it is!

Author: @awkwardplatypus9083
Content:
AI, it’s the new, “everything needs an app,” which was the new, “everything requires an internet connection,” which was the new,“everything needs Bluetooth.”

Someone found a solution to a set of very niche problems, and a board member decided it needed to be everywhere.

No, my microwave shouldn’t require an internet connection. I press buttons, it does the thing, that’s how it should work. What do you mean it needs software updates? It’s a timer, a magnetron, a motor, a door switch, and you might have some preprogrammed buttons and a humidity sensor if you want to be fancy.

No, I don’t need an app for my blender to get the perfect mix. I can watch it, and simply stop it when I want. It takes a few seconds. I don’t even have to take out my phone, open the app, log in because of course I’ll have to, wait for the app to update, struggle to reconnect to the blender, find the right menu in the app because the update moved everything around for the sake of, “user experience,” and FINALLY I can press the button and… why isn’t it working?

No, I don’t need a Bluetooth connection for my power-drill. What’s that even supposed to do? Provide torque monitoring and adaptive power management? Not that you should use the slip chuck settings for drilling, but you can set them without a Bluetooth connection. And power management? My finger, on the trigger, manages the power just fine.

No, I don’t need AI to try to think for me on topics it’s scraping (stealing) data on from people who don’t know what they’re talking about, or grinding knowledgeable people’s words into nonsense. Never mind the inability to separate satire and jokes from facts. Never mind how intrusive it is by the very nature of how it learns!

AI has it’s place. It is very good when you have large amounts of data on a very specific topic that needs to be sorted, characterized, or otherwise interpreted. It’s fantastic when iterative actions by a human are possible, but would be never ending due to the input data stream. This is great for scientific research where you could collect hundreds or even thousands of sample points/graphs/images in a day and going through them by hand would take months to do manually. A trained AI model could interpret them as they’re being collected. (A review of the AI results by a human is still necessary.) It can work wonders for iterative design when there are so many interdependent parameters that it would take multiple engineers multiple lifetimes to make significant improvements.

AI is being used for that, but it’s also, unfortunately, being used to “help” people determine every facet of their lives. It’s being used to collect every bit of everyone’s personal information. It’s being used by students to undermine their education, so they can’t even tell if the AI is wrong or not. It’s being used to make creative works to the point that people who have spent their entire lives crafting their skills are being accused of using AI.

But again, some board member, completely disconnected from the reality of the effects of their decisions, decided it’s a solution to… something… and demanded that everyone else be the guinea pigs.
